chunks: 6. He said: Abu Ja’far Muhammad ibn ‘Ali ibn al-Husayn reported from his father, from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-‘Attar, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from al-Hasan ibn ‘Ali al-Kufi, from al-‘Abbas ibn ‘Amir al-Qasbani, from Ahmad ibn Rizq al-Ghamshani, from Yahya ibn Abi al-‘Ala’, from Jabir, from Abu Ja’far Muhammad ibn ‘Ali, from his father, from his grandfather, peace be upon them, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said:

When the Day of Judgment comes and the inhabitants of Paradise have settled in Paradise and the inhabitants of the Fire in the Fire, a servant will remain in the Fire for seventy autumns — and an autumn is seventy years. Then he will beseech Allah, Mighty and Glorious, and call out: O my Lord, I ask You by the right of Muhammad and the People of his House, have mercy on me. So Allah, exalted be His majesty, will reveal to Jibra’il:
Go down to My servant and bring him out. Jibra’il will say: How can I descend into the Fire? Allah, blessed and exalted, will say to him: I have commanded it to be coolness and safety upon you.

Jibra’il will say: Where is he, and what is my knowledge of his location? Allah will say: He is in a pit of Sijjin. So Jibra’il will descend to the Fire and will find him shackled upon his face. He will bring him out and stand him before Allah. Allah will say: O My servant, how long did you remain in the Fire beseeching Me? He will say: O my Lord, I cannot reckon it. Allah will say to him:

By My might and My majesty, were it not that you asked Me by their right, I would have prolonged your humiliation in the Fire. But it is a decree upon Myself that no servant shall ask Me by the right of Muhammad and the People of his House except that I forgive what is between Me and him.
And I have already forgiven you today. Then he will be commanded to be taken to Paradise.
ai.seo_question: What does Islamic tradition teach about intercession (shafa’a) through the Prophet Muhammad and Ahl al-Bayt on the Day of Judgment?
ai.summary: This prophetic hadith describes the intercession (shafa’a) through the Prophet Muhammad and his household (Ahl al-Bayt) on the Day of Judgment. A servant who has spent seventy autumns in Hellfire beseeches Allah by the right of Muhammad and his family. Allah sends the angel Jibra’il to rescue him from the deepest pit of Hell (Sijjin), making the fire cool and safe for the angel. When brought before Allah, the servant is told that his salvation came solely because he invoked the right of the Prophet and Ahl al-Bayt — a divine decree that guarantees forgiveness to anyone who makes such a plea.

en.mulla-asgharali-m-m-jaffer: 6. He said: Abu Ja’far Muhammad ibn ‘Ali ibn al-Husayn reported from his father, who reported from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar, who reported from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from al-Hasan ibn ‘Ali al-Kufi, from al-Abbas ibn Amir al-Qasbani, from Ahmad ibn Rizq al-Ghamshani, from Yahya ibn Abul Ala’, from Jabir, from Abu Ja’far Muhammad ibn ‘Ali ibn al-Husayn, from his father, from his grandfather, peace be upon them all, who said: The Prophet, peace be upon him and his progeny, said:

"On the Day of Judgement, when the People of Paradise will have settled in their blissful gardens and the people of hell will be in the fire, there will be one who spent seventy autumns in the fire, each autumn is equal to seventy years; then he will beseech Allah, Most High, imploring: "O my Sustainer, I ask you in the name of Muhammad and the inmates of his house to have mercy on me."

Then Allah, Most Mighty, will command Jibraeel, peace be upon him: "Descend to my servant and release him." Jibraeel would say: "How can I descend into hellfire?" Allah, Most Benevolent, would say: "We have commanded the fire to be cold and safe for you."

He (Jibraeel) would say: "O my Sustainer! How do I know where he is located?" Allah would say: "He is in the pit of Sijjin." Then Jibraeel would descend into the fire, find him shackled onto his face, so he will get him out. There he (the servant) stands in the presence of Allah, Most High; then Allah addresses him: "O My servant, for how long have you been in fire, entreating Me thus?" He would say: "I have no count."

Allah, Most High, would say: "By My Honour, had you not beseeched in the name of those, who have a status in My estimation, you would have stayed there in a prolonged humiliation. But, I have ordained for Myself that no one asks me in the name of Muhammad and the inmates of his household, except that I forgive him all that is between Me and him.
So, I have pardoned you today." Then Allah will command for him to be taken to the Paradise.
